sr_hook: Stretch a graph, then flip it over an axis.
sr_stage_aria: Graph of f, stretched and reflected: {title}
sr_step_intro_caption: Same f. This time the whole grid can stretch with it.
sr_step_vertical_caption: a·f(x) stretches every height by a. Points on the x-axis stay put.
sr_step_horizontal_caption: Now the factor goes inside the brackets: f(2x).
sr_step_horizontal_predict_caption: Where does the peak of f(2x) land? Drag the marker there.
sr_step_horizontal_answer_caption: Narrower! f(2x) reaches each height at half the x. The y-axis stays put.
sr_step_reflect_x_caption: Take a through 0 to −1: the graph flattens, then flips. That is −f(x).
sr_step_reflect_y_caption: Now b through 0 to −1: mirrored in the y-axis. That is f(−x).
sr_step_explore_caption: Drag the peak anywhere: up and down is a, sideways is b.
